parsed.why: Low-risk tier: no facility ban, repeated gubernatorial vetoes of anti-trans bills, but no statewide nondiscrimination or hate-crime coverage; restrictive local markers are resident-facing. Shares national passport/entry exposure, so rises only moderately above parent.

Codified gender-identity nondiscrimination, hate-crime coverage, conversion-therapy ban, no facility restriction; sports move advisory only. Robust protections beyond parent average, offset by shared national document and custody regimes.

Strongest local regime: full nondiscrimination, hate-crime enhancements, no facility ban, X markers, court-backed facility access, identity-based prison placement. Only drag is university sports capitulation under national pressure; shared national passport exposure keeps it from higher.

No facility ban; commission regulation with real remedies (damages, stop orders), X markers, city sanctuary order shielding travellers. Offset by absent hate-crime statute and legislature passing sports bills; national document regime still applies.

Adds a tier-1 universal exposure atop the parent: birth-sex facility ban with private cause of action, no nondiscrimination or hate-crime law, restrictive markers, ranked among worst for anti-trans legislation. Materially below parent's 0.35.
